title.narrative: Enhancing Agricultural Resilience (EAR) in Nigeria- CRL Signature Programme

description.narrative:
EYN Projects and ICARE are consortium partners implementing in the Northeast and North West regions of Nigeria, respectively. From the two regions, two outcomes of the signature programme will be achieved. The Enhancing Action and Resilience project will be implemented in two LGAs (Mafa and Shani LGAs) of Borno State by EYN Projects, while ICARE will be implementing it in the Bunkure and Garun Mallam LGAs of Kano State. The two consortium partners will focus on the existing and a new Youth Farmers’ Cooperative, individual entrepreneurial enterprises.
The programme aims to strengthen climate-resilient livelihoods for smallholder farmers through the promotion of practical, affordable, and sustainable climate-smart agricultural systems. The programme will directly support 100 farmers, including persons with disabilities, across Bunkure and Garun Mallam LGAs of Kano State. Of this number, 70% will be male and 30% female, reflecting current participation patterns in farming communities while ensuring inclusive engagement. 70 beneficiaries will be selected from existing cooperatives and farmer groups, while 30 will be individual smallholder farmers, enabling the programme to strengthen both group-based and independent farming systems.
The programme will target Members of farmer cooperatives and producer groups, Individual farmers operating at household level and Community-based savings groups The programme will ensure inclusive participation while focusing on economically active farming households. Expected Effects on Target Groups: ● Improved capacity of youth farmers, cooperatives, and entrepreneurs to produce and commercialise organic inputs and biomass briquettes, leading to increased income and resilience. ● Increased adoption of sustainable practices, such as biomass briquettes and agrosilvopastoral systems, improves livelihoods while reducing environmental degradation. ● Strengthened market access and financial inclusion enhance economic security and business sustainability. ● Increased access to and use of weather information improves farmers’ ability to anticipate and respond to climate shocks. ● Increased use of smart irrigation and climate-resilient inputs supports year-round farming and greater productivity. ● Improved capacity by community structures to drive locally led adaptation and support recovery from climate-related shocks.
